idiom_name: module-level factory function over a plain implementation registry (dynamic import() for lazy stores)
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no factory classes: each DAO is a module, class or object exporting the same method names, and the factory is one function that resolves a store key to an implementation - usually a frozen object map, sometimes await import('./dao/' + store + '.js') for lazily loaded or plugin-provided stores. What replaces the classic structure is the module boundary itself plus the registry object; the store key and the configuration belong to the composition root (the app entry module), never to the DAOs. Frameworks use exactly this shape internally: NestJS providers accept a useFactory function whose return value is the injected DAO.
pitfalls: Store keys are strings: a typo survives until runtime and a missing property yields undefined rather than an error, so freeze the key map or model it as a union in TypeScript.
DAO modules are module-cache singletons: per-tenant state stored in module scope leaks across tenants, so implementations must return instances from the factory instead of keeping state globally.
await import() makes the factory asynchronous and callers must handle promises; mixing synchronous and dynamically loaded registries in one seam produces ordering bugs.
Dynamic specifiers like './dao/' + store + '.js' defeat bundler analysis; keep an explicit map or document the glob so builds include every store.
